analysis: The PR modifies only docs/reference/configuration.md: the date line and the 'Cluster runtime facts' section around head lines 923-1008, with small edits near head lines 1070-1076. It contains no source or security-control changes. The provided units are the base text at 1228-1486 and 1487-1593, which are outside the changed base ranges, and the head text at 1-313, which holds only the date change at line 3. The visible content describes existing behavior (cluster link setup, osascript-approved privileged commands, sandbox CLI, add-on hold, endpoint resumption and logout) and shows no new attack surface or invalidated threat assumptions. The one behavior-relevant documentation change is in the patch excerpt: signed releases can register a `cluster_runtime` block in the `POST /v1/releases` payload, and a coordinator that accepts it derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from it. That touches A-005, A-011 and A-017 (release registration and build trust) and TB-011. The excerpt is truncated, and the head text for lines 923-1008 and 1070-1076 was not supplied, so the exact documented trust model could not be examined. This is a coordinator/platform-owned control and outside the retained scope. The threat model may need an update if provider-side code consumes these auto-derived approvals, because it would shift trust from the operator approval file to release-publication integrity. That is unverified. I flag it for a later pass, not as a finding. No concrete regression is supported by the supplied evidence.
